spelling_programme_year_2.title: The '-ge' and '-dge' spelling at the end of words
spelling_programme_year_2.learning_point: The '-dge' spelling is used straight after short vowel sounds (a, e, i, o, u like in badge or bridge). The '-ge' spelling is used after other sounds (like in age, badge vs cage).
spelling_programme_year_2.rule_mnemonic: Short vowel? Add 'dge'! (badge, hedge). Long vowel or consonant? Just '-ge'! (cage, large).

words.example: She wore a shiny gold badge on her coat.
Don't stand too close to the edge.
The train crossed the river on a high bridge.
He can dodge the ball quickly in gym class.
Grandma made delicious chocolate fudge.
What age will you be on your next birthday?
An elephant is a huge animal.
We change our shoes before PE.
Please charge the tablet battery.
They live in a quiet seaside village.

dictation_sentences: The badge fell off the edge of the high bridge.
We can change into our boots in the huge village.

spelling_programme_year_2.title: The '-c' sound spelled '-c' before e, i and y ('Soft C')
spelling_programme_year_2.phonics_focus: The /s/ sound spelled c before e, i, y
spelling_programme_year_2.learning_point: When 'c' comes before 'e', 'i' or 'y', it makes a soft /s/ sound instead of a hard /k/ sound.
spelling_programme_year_2.rule_mnemonic: C before E, I, or Y makes a soft /s/ sound like ice!

words.example: Run fast to win the playground race.
Put ice into the cold water glass.
A honeycomb cell holds sweet honey.
London is a busy capital city.
She wore a fancy party dress.
Rockets blast off into outer space.
Draw a neat round circle.
We love to dance to joyful music.
Sharpen your wooden pencil for writing.
The prince lived in a grand castle.

dictation_sentences: Draw a circle in pencil on the fancy paper.
We race in the city near outer space.

spelling_programme_year_2.title: The '-kn-' and '-gn-' silent letter spellings
spelling_programme_year_2.phonics_focus: The /n/ sound spelled kn and gn at word start
spelling_programme_year_2.learning_point: The letters 'k' and 'g' are silent when paired with 'n' at the beginning of these words.
spelling_programme_year_2.rule_mnemonic: Knock knock! The K is silent when N is near!

words.example: Knock on the door before entering.
I know all the answers to the spelling quiz.
Bend your knee to sit down comfortably.
Cut the bread carefully with a butter knife.
A tiny gnat buzzed near the garden light.
Puppies like to gnaw on chew toys.
The brave knight rode a white horse.
Tie a tight knot in your shoe laces.
Grandma can knit a warm cozy scarf.
A cute garden gnome stands by the flowers.

dictation_sentences: The knight had a knot in his shiny armor.
I know how to knit a scarf for the gnome.

spelling_programme_year_2.title: The '-wr-' silent letter spelling at word start
spelling_programme_year_2.learning_point: When 'w' comes before 'r' at the start of a word, the 'w' is silent.
spelling_programme_year_2.rule_mnemonic: W is quiet when writing with R!

words.example: Write your full name at the top of the paper.
The story was written in a famous book.
If an answer is wrong, try again!
Wrap the birthday present with colorful paper.
Wear a digital watch on your wrist.
The old shipwreck lay deep under water.
A small wren sang a song in the oak tree.
Wring the wet cloth before cleaning.
Worms wriggle through moist garden soil.
Playful cubs wrestle on the grass.

dictation_sentences: Write carefully so you do not get it wrong.
Wrap the cloth around your injured wrist.

spelling_programme_year_2.title: The '-le' spelling at the end of words
spelling_programme_year_2.learning_point: The '-le' spelling is the most common way to spell the /əl/ sound at the end of Year 2 words.
spelling_programme_year_2.rule_mnemonic: Most end /əl/ words love '-le' like table, apple, smile!

words.example: Place the books neatly on the study table.
Eat a crunchy red apple for morning snack.
Fill your water bottle before playing outdoor sports.
A little kitten napped in the sun beam.
Stand right in the middle of the group circle.
Blow a gigantic soapy bubble into the breeze.
Light a birthday candle on the cake.
Build a tall sand castle at the beach.
This math puzzle has a simple step solution.
My uncle came to visit our family.

dictation_sentences: Put the little apple on the clean table.
Blow a bubble near the castle candle.

spelling_programme_year_2.title: The '-el' spelling at the end of words
spelling_programme_year_2.phonics_focus: The /əl/ sound spelled -el after m, n, r, v, w
spelling_programme_year_2.learning_point: The '-el' spelling is used after specific consonants like m, n, r, v, w or words like camel and tunnel.
spelling_programme_year_2.rule_mnemonic: Camel, travel, towel, angel! '-el' makes these words fly!

words.example: The camel walked across the warm desert dunes.
The train sped through the dark mountain tunnel.
A nimble squirrel buried an acorn in autumn.
We love to travel to new cities during summer.
Dry your hands with a soft clean towel.
The hazel tree produced crunchy hazelnuts.
A, E, I, O, U are the five main vowels.
The angel topper shone brightly on the tree.
The crown sparkled with a red ruby jewel.
Silver tinsel shimmered on the holiday tree.

dictation_sentences: The camel ran into the dark train tunnel.
Use a dry towel after you travel home.

interactive_components.week_carousel: Smooth Embla/Framer-motion powered weekly card carousel with instant week indicator dots, quick jumping keyboard navigation (Arrow keys), and Week 1 auto-selection for 7th Sept 2026.
interactive_components.practice_mode: Interactive Spelling Audio & Flashcard Quiz mode with simulated Speech Synthesis (TTS web API / custom audio trigger), typing input validation, and instant particle celebratory confetti feedback.
interactive_components.printable_view: Clean high-contrast printable layout generator. Formats spelling list + phonics rule + dictation sentences into an A4 print-ready worksheet with user student name header.
interactive_components.parent_teacher_notes: Tabbed interactive panel with downloadable teacher guidelines, home practice tips, phonics breakdown diagram, and weekly progress tracker modal.

component_strategy.marketing_sections: Use raw React + Tailwind + Framer Motion for custom glass cards, glowing borders, kinetic hero typography, marquee strip, and printable layout overlay.
component_strategy.interactive_widgets: Use Shadcn Tabs, Dialog, DropdownMenu, Tooltip, Progress, Accordion, and Toast (Sonner) heavily styled to fit Cyber Void theme.
component_strategy.testing_requirement: Every interactive button, tab, card, carousel navigation link, print button, practice input, audio button, and week badge MUST include a explicit `data-testid` attribute in kebab-case.

instructions_to_main_agent: Build a stunning, Awwwards Site-of-the-Day level Year 2 Spelling Programme web application.
Treat September 7, 2026 as Week 1 start date today in the application UI logic.
Ensure Week 1 ('-dge' and '-ge') is active on initial page launch, with seamless navigation to Weeks 2-6 and full term selector.
Implement the kinetic hero banner with line-by-line masked text reveal, floating holographic 3D letter block widget (using CSS 3D or SVG parallax canvas), and live countdown to W/C 7 Sept 2026.

Provide an interactive weekly carousel card system displaying words with phonics highlighting, phonetic spelling, audio pronunciation button (using SpeechSynthesis API), sample sentences, and challenge words.
Include a 'Practice & Quiz Mode' modal/tab where students can test their spelling with instant particle confetti feedback and audio prompts.
Include a 'Printable Weekly List' view triggered by a button that hides non-essential UI and presents an elegant A4 printable worksheet layout.
Include a robust 'Parent & Teacher Notes' section with phonics explanation, dictation practice sentences, weekly learning point summary, and home practice tips.
Ensure dark/light theme toggle is active and both themes strictly adhere to WCAG AA contrast rules.
Ensure all interactive elements have explicit `data-testid` attributes.

UNIVERSAL GUIDELINES FOR MAIN AGENT.avoid_ai_slop: Never use default Vercel white/black card templates or centered boring layouts. Layer elements with z-index, glowing border strokes, glassmorphism, and micro-interactions.
UNIVERSAL GUIDELINES FOR MAIN AGENT.no_universal_transition: Do NOT apply universal transition (transition: all) as it breaks transforms and framer-motion animations.
UNIVERSAL GUIDELINES FOR MAIN AGENT.no_centered_app: Do NOT center align the app container. Maintain left-aligned narrative hierarchy for text.
UNIVERSAL GUIDELINES FOR MAIN AGENT.no_emojis_for_icons: Use Lucide icons (Volume2, Printer, Sparkles, BookOpen, ChevronRight, Calendar, Award, CheckCircle2) instead of emoji characters.
UNIVERSAL GUIDELINES FOR MAIN AGENT.spacing: Use generous Tailwind spacing (p-6, p-8, p-12, gap-8) to prevent cramped designs.
UNIVERSAL GUIDELINES FOR MAIN AGENT.toasts: Use Sonner toast notifications for actions like 'Copied word list', 'Print ready', and 'Quiz completed'.
